title: Old vs New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC / Section 202)
source: Income Tax Department, Government of India (Income Tax Act 1961 & Income Tax Act 2025)
reference: Section 115BAC, Income Tax Act 1961 — recodified as Section 202 under Income Tax Act 2025
content: The New Tax Regime under Section 115BAC (recodified as Section 202 under the Income Tax Act 2025) is the default tax regime for individuals and HUFs. Under the New Tax Regime for Tax Year 2026-27, the 7-bracket income tax slab structure is: ₹0 to ₹4,00,000 (Nil), ₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 (5%), ₹8,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 (10%), ₹12,00,001 to ₹16,00,000 (15%), ₹16,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 (20%), ₹20,00,001 to ₹24,00,000 (25%), and Above ₹24,00,000 (30%). The New Regime offers lower tax slab rates but foregoes major Chapter VI-A deductions (Section 80C / Section 123, Section 80D / Section 126, HRA / Schedule III). However, ₹75,000 Standard Deduction and employer NPS Section 80CCD(2) remain deductible under the New Regime. With the Section 87A (recodified as Section 157) rebate up to ₹60,000 for taxable income up to ₹12,00,000, taxpayers with ₹9 lakh income (or 9 lakh annual income) pay ₹0 tax under the New Regime. Under the Old Tax Regime, slab rates are higher (0-2.5L 0%, 2.5L-5L 5%, 5L-10L 20%, >10L 30%), but taxpayers can claim 80C, 80D, HRA, and home loan deductions.
